en.headline: Police arrest two over alleged sedition near Prince Edward
en.dek: Authorities said a 37-year-old man and a 58-year-old woman were detained on Wednesday in a case linked to an August gathering outside the MTR station.
body: Police arrested two people on Wednesday for allegedly acting with seditious intent, in an operation the force linked to a gathering outside Prince Edward MTR station on 31 August. A police statement identified the suspects only as a 37-year-old man and a 58-year-old woman. Local media, including a report carried by Hong Kong Free Press, identified them as independent journalist Tang Ho-wing and activist Lee Ying-chi. Neither has been charged.

The force said officers found several people outside the station that evening holding bouquets and shouting what police described as seditious slogans. Six other people were arrested earlier this month over the same alleged offence and have since been released on bail, the statement said. Police also said some people at the scene were suspected of spreading false information and attacking the government.

The pair were detained for investigation under the local national security law passed in 2024, according to the Hong Kong Free Press report. If convicted of the alleged offence, they could face up to seven years in prison. The Hong Kong Journalists Association said Tang's arrest was the first publicly known case of a journalist being arrested for sedition under that law, and said reporting was not sedition.

Police said the 2019 claims about the Prince Edward station incident were unfounded. Tang, who runs the online outlet Boom News, had posted a video from outside the station showing people shouting the date, the report said. The Committee to Protect Journalists called for his release. The force has not announced any charge.

zh.headline: 警方拘兩人 指涉太子站外煽動意圖
zh.dek: 警方稱周三拘捕37歲男子及58歲女子，案件與8月31日太子站外聚集有關；兩人尚未被控。
body: 警方周三拘捕兩人，指他們涉嫌以煽動意圖行事，行動與8月31日太子港鐵站外的聚集有關。警方通報只稱嫌疑人為37歲男子及58歲女子。本地媒體包括《香港自由新聞》轉載的報道，指兩人分別是獨立記者鄧皓榮及社運人士李盈姿。兩人尚未被控。
警方稱，當晚在站外發現有人持花束並高叫警方形容為煽動的口號。同案較早前另有六人被捕，其後已保釋。警方又稱，現場有人涉嫌散播虛假信息及攻擊政府。
《香港自由新聞》報道指，兩人根據2024年本地國安法被扣查。若罪名成立，可判處最高七年監禁。記協表示，這是公開所知首宗記者因該法下的煽動罪被捕，並指採訪不是煽動。
警方稱2019年有關太子站事件的說法並不屬實。報道指，經營網上媒體「爆新聞」的鄧皓榮曾在站外拍片，片中有人高叫日期。保護記者委員會呼籲釋放他。警方尚未宣布任何檢控。
